claims.text: Between 600 and 800°C, the overall wear resistance of an FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating is governed by formation of a high-entropy oxide scale.
The proposed high-entropy oxide scale is stable, adherent, and self-healing.
Controlled pre-oxidation promotes formation of the oxide scale through thermally activated elemental diffusion.
The oxide scale reduces subsequent material removal and abrasion during high-temperature service.
The baseline is an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating on a conventional metal substrate without pre-oxidation.
The proposed intervention is pre-oxidation at approximately 650°C for 30 minutes.
Elevated-temperature pre-oxidation enhances diffusion of specific alloying elements.
Specific alloying elements preferentially form a high-entropy oxide scale at the coating surface.
The surface oxide minimizes direct sliding contact by reducing the effective attacking area.
The oxide provides a continuous, self-replenishing barrier against wear.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have a statistically significantly lower wear rate than as-deposited coatings during testing at 600–800°C.
Pre-oxidized coatings will exhibit smoother or otherwise improved wear-track morphology compared with the as-deposited baseline.
The proposed mechanism is limited to wear testing between 600 and 800°C under representative mechanical loading.
Behavior outside the 600–800°C regime may not follow the proposed oxide-mediated mechanism.
Failure to detect a well-defined high-entropy oxide scale on the pre-oxidized coating would falsify the hypothesis.
